name: Impact, capacity and tap fees
summary: Development impact fees and water/sewer capacity (tap) fees, by land use. The national baseline is the Duncan Associates National Impact Fee Survey: 2019 (270 jurisdictions), the most recent public national survey; values are in 2019 dollars and the build script escalates them. Important: survey averages cover only jurisdictions that charge fees, so mids use the national average EXCLUDING California (CA fees are 2-4x the rest of the country and belong in regional evidence). Fees are extremely local — the engine should treat these as a placeholder the user overrides with the local schedule.

items.name: Total impact fees — single-family detached

range.method: Mid = Duncan 2019 national average excluding California, $9,841 (e1). High = national average including California, $13,627 (e1, same figure in NAHB primer e8). Low = first quartile of the 34 state averages on the survey's state sheet, $3,158 (computed from e2). Includes utility (water/sewer) impact fees. | Second pass (2026-10-24): Mid recalibrated to the NAHB 2024 Cost of Constructing a Home average impact fee of $6,367 (residential/single-family.json#e10). The Duncan 2019 survey average ($9,841, ex-CA) covers only jurisdictions that charge fees and, escalated with a construction-cost index, roughly doubles a national average; it is kept as evidence for the upper range. Range $3,000–$14,000 brackets both.

items.notes: Standard unit: 3-BR, 2,000 SF on a 10,000 SF lot. NAHB inflated the 2019 average to ~$16,394 in 2024 dollars with ENR CCI (e8). California averages $37,471 (e2).

items.name: Total impact fees — multifamily unit

range.method: Mid = Duncan 2019 national average excluding California, $5,864 (e3); high = national average incl. CA, $8,034; low = first quartile of the 34 state averages, ~$2,030 (computed from the survey's multi-family state sheet).

items.notes: Standard unit: 2-BR, 1,000 SF at 12 units/acre. California cities run $12,000-$75,000/unit in total development fees (Terner, e9).

range.method: Mid = national average excl. CA $5,228/1,000 SF; high = national average $6,760; low = first quartile of 33 state averages ~$2,282 (e4). Road fees dominate ($5,970 of the national average).
Mid = national average excl. CA $4,178/1,000 SF; high = national average $5,408; low = first quartile of 33 state averages ~$1,516 (e5).
Mid = national average excl. CA $3,147/1,000 SF; high = national average $3,942; low = first quartile of 33 state averages ~$1,163 (e6).

The national survey has no lodging category. Derived: office fee $4,178 per 1,000 SF (e5) x ~0.6 (about 600 gross SF per key) = ~$2,500/room; bracketed by roughly 0.2x-0.6x of a multifamily unit fee (e3) on the low side and 1.2x office on the high side. Low confidence — many schedules charge hotels per room mainly for roads.

items.name: Water capacity / tap / impact fee

range.method: One single-family unit = 1 EDU. Mid = Duncan 2019 single-family water fee, national average excl. CA, $3,603 (e1; incl. CA $4,249, n=128). Low/high = first and third quartile of the 22 state water averages ($1,887 / $5,271) computed from the state sheet (e2). | Second pass (2026-10-24): Mid recalibrated so water + sewer per EDU equals the NAHB 2024 survey's 'water and sewer fees/inspections' of $6,260 per single-family home (1 EDU; residential/single-family.json#e10), split evenly between water and sewer (the split is derived). Duncan 2019 per-EDU averages are kept as evidence for the high end.

items.notes: Excludes meter set and service-line installation charges. Some utilities price by meter size, not EDU.

items.name: Sewer (wastewater) capacity / tap / impact fee

range.method: Mid = Duncan 2019 single-family wastewater fee, national average excl. CA, $3,420 (e1; incl. CA $3,896, n=138). Low/high = first and third quartile of the 27 state sewer averages ($1,843 / $5,135) from the state sheet (e2). | Second pass (2026-10-24): Mid recalibrated so water + sewer per EDU equals the NAHB 2024 survey's 'water and sewer fees/inspections' of $6,260 per single-family home (1 EDU; residential/single-family.json#e10), split evenly between water and sewer (the split is derived). Duncan 2019 per-EDU averages are kept as evidence for the high end.

items.notes: Phoenix shows how large utility fees can be: $22,157 water + $12,486 sewer for a single-family unit in 2019 (e10).

range.method: Definition: one equivalent dwelling unit (EDU/ERU) = one single-family detached home on a standard (3/4-inch or 5/8-inch) meter.

items.name: EDU conversion — multifamily unit

range.method: Implied by the 2019 national averages: multifamily/single-family water fee $1,680/$4,249 = 0.40 and sewer $1,986/$3,896 = 0.51 (e1, e3). Many utility schedules (not fetched) assign 0.5-0.8 ERU per apartment; mid 0.6 sits between the survey-implied ~0.45 and common schedule values. Verify locally.

items.notes: Senior and studio units sit at the low end; townhomes near 1.0.

items.name: EDU conversion — nonresidential per 1,000 SF

range.method: Ratios of 2019 national average utility fees per 1,000 SF to the single-family fee: retail water 654/4,249 = 0.15, sewer 852/3,896 = 0.22; office 855/4,249 = 0.20, 1,217/3,896 = 0.31; industrial 889/4,249 = 0.21, 1,662/3,896 = 0.43 (e1, e4-e6). Mid 0.25 ~ median of the six ratios.

items.notes: Restaurants, car washes, laundries and process users are far higher; utilities usually size these by meter or fixture units.

evidence.quote: Single-Family Unit sheet (page 4 of 20): National Average $13,627 total, $9,887 non-utility, $4,249 water, $3,896 sewer; National Avg w/o CA $9,841 total, $3,603 water, $3,420 sewer; sample size 270.
evidence.scopeNotes: Average of jurisdictions that charge impact fees (not of all jurisdictions); includes water/wastewater capacity fees. Standard 3-BR, 2,000 SF unit.

evidence.quote: State Average Fees, single-family (page 4 of 20): CA $37,471; WA $16,079; CO $12,337; FL $10,878; AZ $10,068; TX $6,906; GA $2,735; MO $900.

evidence.quote: Multi-Family Unit sheet (page 8 of 20): National Average $8,034 total, $1,680 water, $1,986 sewer; National Avg w/o CA $5,864; state averages CA $21,703, FL $7,774, CO $6,915, AZ $4,325.
evidence.scopeNotes: 2-BR, 1,000 SF unit, 12 units/acre, 240-unit complex. First quartile of state averages ~$2,030 (computed).

an “average impact fee” must be understood as an average fee for those communities that charge impact fees, not as an average for all communities.
evidence.scopeNotes: Why the engine should let the user zero these out where no fees apply.
